title: Two Days of U.S. Strikes in Iran Signal a Sharp Escalation
partialText: U.S. forces hit more than 170 targets, including air defense systems, drone and missile storage sites, and military speedboats.

title: The U.S. and Iran Are Fighting Again. Is the Cease-Fire Over?
partialText: Eric Schmitt, a New York Times National Security correspondent, analyzes recent skirmishes between the U.S. and Iran and whether they threaten ongoing negotiations for a peace deal.

title: Iran’s Supreme Leader Remains Absent, a Void at the Top of the Regime
partialText: Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei did not appear at his father’s funeral this week, fueling speculation about his physical condition and leaving a power vacuum in a divided country.

title: Mediators Trying to Pull U.S. and Iran Back From Brink, Officials Say
partialText: Qatari mediators were in Iran seeking to salvage the tattered truce. President Trump said talks with Tehran would continue, even if the cease-fire was “over.”

title: New Air Force One Lacks Defensive Countermeasures of Previous Model, Officials Say
partialText: Experts said the lack of such capabilities poses a potential risk when the president travels overseas. The White House defended the aircraft’s safety.

title: Trump Administration Fires Members of Independent Election Group
partialText: The firings and a resignation render the Election Assistance Commission useless. The moves come as President Trump seeks to impose control over how ballots will be counted in the midterms.

title: Witnesses of ICE Killing in Houston Dispute the Official Account
partialText: The agency said a Mexican immigrant driving a van tried to ram agents before they shot him dead. A lawyer for three passengers said that was untrue.

title: At Least 21 People Have Been Shot by Federal Immigration Agents Since Last Year
partialText: Many of them have been shot in their cars. Five have died, including three U.S. citizens. Here are their names and what we know about the circumstances.

title: Why Some Women in Maine Are Mourning the End of Graham Platner’s Campaign
partialText: They believe the accuser, but they also grieve the demise of a campaign that promised that politics could be different — and they blame those who failed to find a less flawed candidate.

title: Eight Years Later, They’re Still Restoring a House Bought at Auction
partialText: First-time buyers from the Bay Area won an abandoned house at a Kingston, N.Y., tax auction. Eight years later, they’re still restoring it.

title: An Aging Assassin Was Caught by ICE. Will the U.S. Deport Him?
partialText: He helped plot a car bombing in Washington that killed two people in 1976. Fifty years later, old government secrets could decide his fate.

title: The Work of Helping A.I. Destroy Work
partialText: Start-ups are paying white-collar professionals to teach their jobs to artificial intelligence models. It’s a bonanza. It’s bleak. Where will it end?

title: How Terrorist Groups Are Using A.I. to Gain an Edge in Battle
partialText: A.I. chatbots are not just a propaganda tool for violent extremists but are aiding in bomb construction and attack planning, new research finds.

title: A.I. Has Rewarded Investors. It May Now Pose Their Greatest Risk.
partialText: Near the midpoint of the year, stocks and bonds both report good returns. But the global stock market has become highly concentrated, our columnist says.

title: Trump Is Promoting ‘Freedom Fuel’ for $3.47 a Gallon. Who’s Behind It?
partialText: The president has praised a network of 25 recently rebranded gas stations in the Philadelphia region that have been selling gas for considerably less than the national average.

title: China Launches Reusable Rocket, Clearing a Key Hurdle in Race With SpaceX
partialText: The launch and recovery of the Long March 10B could represent a long-awaited breakthrough for Chinese satellite companies.

title: How Volkswagen’s Troubles Were Made in China
partialText: The German auto giant’s push into China powered it for decades, but now the company faces fierce competition from Chinese automakers in markets around the world.

title: This Star Just Ate a Planet, and It’s Not Done Yet
partialText: A star 1,300 light-years away appears to have just consumed one world and is gearing up for seconds.

title: A Chinese Spacecraft Captures First Image of Quasi-Moon
partialText: A Chinese spacecraft has captured the first image of the asteroid Kamo‘oalewa.

title: This Is a Lot More Worrying Than the Supreme Court’s Ruling on Executive Power
partialText: The White House is sidestepping Congress to make huge decisions for even the most important private industries.

title: The Very Good and Very Bad News on Climate
partialText: Advancements in renewable energy are paving the way for a new climate politics. The environmentalist Bill McKibben articulates some of the possibilities in this new era of energy abundance.

title: The Housing Crisis
partialText: Happy Friday. I want to tell you about a rare instance of bipartisan cooperation in Congress.

title: Bayeux Tapestry Arrives in U.K. After Maximum-Security Operation
partialText: The 11th-century tapestry will go on display at the British Museum in September. Tickets for the exhibition have already been selling rapidly.
